in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I have a 3-year-old, Alex, and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 3-year-old child named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few questions:

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now, do you live with Alex, or are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards their upkeep - you know, helping with clothes, food, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To clarify further - approximately how much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each month (or week)? 

Also, who does Alex currently live with, and is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £50 a week towards Alex's needs. Alex lives with their other parent, but as far as I know, they're not claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

1. Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status in the UK?

2. Is there any arrangement where your local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, so no immigration issues there. And no, the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance - it's just me contributing the £50 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Just to confirm one final detail:

You mentioned Alex lives with their other parent. Has Alex been living with the other parent continuously, or did this arrangement start recently? I ask because there are specific rules about how long Child Benefit can continue when a child goes to live with someone else.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been living with their other parent for a while now - it's been the arrangement for some time. It's not a recent change or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ **Alex meets the age requirement** - At 3 years old, Alex is well under the age limit of 16 (or 20 if in approved education/training)

✓ **You meet the residency requirements** - You're a UK citizen living in the UK

✓ **You're considered responsible for Alex** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £50 per week towards their upkeep (clothes, food, etc.). This exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount, which means you qualify as being responsible for the child under the rules

✓ **No one else is claiming** - You've confirmed that Alex's other parent is not currently claiming Child Benefit

✓ **No local council support** - There's no local council payment towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

**Important points to note:**

- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so as long as no one else claims for Alex, you should be able to receive it
- You'll need to continue making regular contributions towards Alex's upkeep to maintain eligibility
- If your income (or your partner's if you have one) is over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

Would you like information on how to make your claim?
